    Meta-regression model specification for parsnip

    Source: R/parsnip-models.R
    meta_linear.Rd

    meta_linear() defines a mixed-effects meta-regression for use with parsnip, workflows and tune. The outcome is the effect size and the predictors are study level moderators. The inverse sampling variances enter as case weights, for example with hardhat::importance_weights(1 / vi); if no case weights are given, a column named .vi in the training data is used.

    Usage

    meta_linear(mode = "regression", engine = "reml")

    Arguments

    mode

    A single character string for the model mode. Only "regression" is available.

    engine

    A single character string for the engine: "reml", "dl" or "fe".

    Value

    A meta_linear model specification.

    Engines

    "reml"

    Random effects with \(\tau^2\) estimated by restricted maximum likelihood (the default).

    "dl"

    Random effects with the DerSimonian-Laird estimator.

    "fe"

    Common effect (fixed effect) meta-regression.

    Examples

    library(parsnip)
bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg
)
spec <- meta_linear(engine = "reml")
spec
#> Meta-regression model specification (regression)
#> 
#> Computational engine: reml
fitted <- fit(spec, .yi ~ ablat, data = bcg)
predict(fitted, new_data = data.frame(ablat = c(10, 40)))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 1
#>     .pred
#>     <dbl>
#> 1 -0.0395
#> 2 -0.913
